LESSON: PATTERN WRITING

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.5: Pattern Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Pattern Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What materials can children use class. • Learners could be engaged in tracing to form line patterns?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Use ICT devices to make simple line patterns. 3.

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PATTERN WRITING
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Pattern Writing helps you succeed in LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: PATTERN WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Use ICT devices to make simple line patterns. 3.

What this means
In this part you learn to Use ICT devices to make simple line patterns. 3.. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Use ICT devices to make simple line patterns. 3..
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Pattern Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Use ICT devices to make simple line patterns. 3.. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Pattern Writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Pattern Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: Use ICT devices to make simple line patterns. 3.)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Pattern Writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: Use ICT devices to make simple line patterns. 3..
3. Make one local Kenya example of Pattern Writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Pattern Writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Pattern Writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What materials can children use class. • Learners could be engaged in tracing to form line patterns?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Pattern Writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: Use ICT devices to make simple line patterns. 3..

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
